subject: Adjudication request — candidate Daniel Cho: conflicting interviewer recommendations
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Adjudication request — Daniel Cho candidate feedback conflict

Neha / Marissa —

I need HR support to adjudicate a feedback discrepancy for a strong backend candidate, Daniel Cho (applied for Senior Software Engineer, infra team). We have mixed recommendations across interviews and an external offer timeline that's tightening. Summary: 

- Technical: Marcus gave a strong technical score and recommended moving to final loop.
- Behavioral: Laura's behavioral debrief flags a red-flag around collaboration / ambiguity in prior role; she recommends we not extend.
- Candidate has an external verbal offer from Infinite AI (Simon Graves) with an intent to sign; timeline says they want an answer by 2026-10-09.

I attached the interview pack and raw notes (interviewer-notes.txt). Laura's writeup contains some phrasing that I agree is blunt; I think it may be resolvable by clarifying examples rather than outright decline. Given the hiring bar and our need on infra, I'm inclined to move forward with an offer at L4 with a small countermove if we can remove overly opinionated language from the record and document a remediation plan (if needed).

Can HR weigh in on: 
1) Whether the behavioral concerns as written constitute a formal disqualifier per policy (Laura and I disagree).
2) Options for next steps: (a) proceed to offer, but add a manager coaching plan in the onboarding; (b) request an explicit follow-up behavioral interview with a neutral interviewer; or (c) decline and document rationales.
3) If we proceed to offer, can HR draft a short verbal + written offer and confirm compensation range (we have budget to be flexible within band).

Timing is tight — need a decision or next-step plan by EOD Monday 2026-10-05 so we can respond before their deadline.

Thanks,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Adjudication request — Daniel Cho candidate feedback conflict

Vivek —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. I reviewed the notes quickly. A few immediate items: 

- Please confirm that we have candidate consent to share the full feedback (we should not send anything beyond what the candidate consents to). If you don't have explicit consent, Marissa can trigger that call.
- Laura's behavioral write-up uses phrases like "doesn't collaborate" and "avoids ownership" — we need concrete examples. If those cannot be substantiated, we should rephrase to measurable behaviors or remove non-evidentiary language.
- Under our hiring policy, a single interviewer can block if they provide clear examples of risk. The question is whether Laura's note meets that bar. I will review the notes and provide an HR assessment, but I need the raw notes in the format shown in the attachment (good).

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Marissa to call Daniel to request permission to share the feedback with him and to gauge counter-offer pressure (Marissa, can you do this today?).
2) If consent granted, Vivek to provide a short (2–3 question) behavioral follow-up for a neutral interviewer to ask; we can schedule this within 48 hours.
3) HR (me) will adjudicate after the follow-up or provide a formal guidance if follow-up isn't possible.

If you are leaning toward offering, tell me the level and proposed base range so I can draft language and confirm approvals.

Neha
HRBP
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Adjudication request — Daniel Cho candidate feedback conflict

Thanks Neha. Quick answers and more context below.

- Consent: I have not asked the candidate yet — please have Marissa reach out.
- Level/band: I'm prepared to move forward at L4 (senior) with a top-of-band base offer at $200k + equity commensurate with L4. Candidate indicated they are targeting ~210–220k total comp externally.

Quoted excerpts from the notes (verbatim, for adjudication):
- "Interviewer A: Technical strong, depth in systems design, handed well on tracing and storage scaling. Recommends final loop; no concerns."
- "Interviewer B (Laura): Candidate described a previous project where ownership was passed between teams; candidate framed it as 'I shipped my part' but lacked examples of cross-team follow-through. Felt like candidate prefers individual contributor scope. Recommends do not extend at this time."

My read: Laura's phrasing includes interpretation words ("felt like", "prefers") without concrete examples — we can either ask Laura to add a short example of a behavioral incident or run one short focused behavioral question (30–40 min) with a neutral interviewer. I prefer the latter to resolve quickly. If HR advises the behavioral concerns are borderline and a follow-up would likely clear, proceed with the follow-up. If HR says the note is a clear block, we'll step back.

Given the external offer timeline (deadline 2026-10-09), my preferred path:
1) Marissa calls candidate today to get consent and confirm timeline.
2) If candidate agrees, schedule a 35–40 minute behavioral follow-up this week with a senior PM or Eng manager (neutral).
3) If follow-up clears, HR to sign off and Marissa + I to extend a verbal offer immediately followed by written.

Please confirm you can support this and, Marissa, confirm if you can reach Daniel today. I can take the hiring manager call with him if needed.

Vivek
